q7.answer: On confirm, in one transaction: the pending secret moves into totp_secret_sealed and the pending column is cleared, totp_enabled becomes true, totp_last_step is set to the accepted step, all old recovery_codes rows are deleted and 10 new hashes inserted, and all other sessions of the user are deleted (the current one stays). The raw codes are returned only in that response. I specified a single transaction, so a partway failure would roll back and leave the old state; I did not spell out the failure response beyond that.

q8.answer: It is the login_challenges table (token_hash PK, user_id, expires_at = creation + 5 minutes, attempts). The browser holds the raw token in a separate httponly, secure, Lax 'mfa' cookie, and only its hash is stored. It is removed on a valid entry (row deleted, cookie cleared), on the 5th wrong entry (row deleted), or when found expired on use (purged periodically). No session exists meanwhile.

q9.answer: All on the users row: active secret in totp_secret_sealed (sealed), pending secret in totp_pending_sealed (sealed, ignored by sign-in), replay guard in totp_last_step, and an explicit totp_enabled boolean. Recovery codes are rows in recovery_codes (user_id, code_hash, used_at), hashes only. '2FA on' is determined by totp_enabled, which becomes true only when a valid code from the pending secret is confirmed.

q10.answer: Sign-in keeps using the old active secret and old recovery codes, since the replacement is only in the pending column and totp_enabled stays true. Starting replacement requires re-entering the password. If the user abandons it or cancels, the pending secret is simply ignored or cleared, and the old secret and codes stay active. I did not design an automatic expiry for an abandoned pending secret.

q11.answer: By format: an entry matching the recovery-code format (about 10 base32 characters) is checked as a recovery code, and anything else as a TOTP code. Yes, wrong recovery codes (unknown or already used) count as wrong entries, incrementing attempts atomically, with the challenge discarded at the 5th.
